Hi Marcus / Evelyn,

We have a scheduled DR dry-run next week and Legal asked me to confirm how Redwood handles deletion requests that overlap with backups and cross-region replicas. A couple of concrete questions:

- If we submit a deletion request for dataset acme-cust-42 via the Console API, how soon will that object be removed from: (a) the primary live store, (b) nightly snapshots, and (c) cross-region replicas?
- Do snapshots/sweep jobs keep tombstoned copies longer than the standard retention window?
- If we put a legal hold on a workspace, does that suspend all backup lifecycle sweeps or only the deletion of metadata?
- We also need to understand if KMS key rotation or key destruction can impact our ability to provide a Proof of Deletion for auditors.

We are on a Dedicated plan, and the account team said there may be tenant-specific retention overrides. Can you outline the expected timelines and the process to request an expedited purge (if legally required)?

We'd like to do a short sync and a dry-run of the delete+restore flow before the DR exercise. Can you propose next steps?

Subject: RE: Question on backup retention / deletion propagation before DR dry-run

Hi Elena — thanks for the detailed questions. I spoke with Infra and Compliance to get the canonical answers. Below is a concise summary and an action plan for the dry-run.

Summary (high level)
- Primary live store: deletion requests via Console/API mark objects for logical deletion immediately; metadata is updated within seconds.
- Snapshot/backup retention: snapshots are immutable by default for the snapshot retention window. Deletion requests create a tombstone record; snapshots taken before deletion will continue to contain the older data until those snapshots hit their retention TTL and are swept.
- Cross-region replicas: replication is async. Metadata changes propagate quickly (usually within minutes to hours), but physical block-level compaction/garbage-collection can lag. Typical full propagation to all physical stores is up to 7 days in the worst-case for standard Dedicated tenants.
- Tombstone vs physical purge: we distinguish logical deletion (tombstone) from physical erasure. Tombstones are used for auditability and can be held longer if a legal hold is applied. Physical erasure (secure overwrite/crypto-erase) is performed during the GC window and subject to KMS lifecycle constraints.

Dedicated vs Hosted differences
- Hosted (standard): we enforce the platform default: metadata removal within 24–72h, physical GC within 30 days (unless retention policy extends it).
- Dedicated (your case): retention windows can be configured per-tenant. Your account currently has a 90-day snapshot TTL and 365-day cold backup retention. That means snapshots older than 90 days are eligible for sweep, but cold backups are maintained for 365 days unless a purge is requested.

Legal hold behavior
- Placing a legal hold on a workspace flips an internal flag that prevents both snapshot sweep and physical GC for any object in scope. Metadata deletion will be blocked; tombstones are not applied while the hold is active.
- Holds are tenant-scoped, and the support/legal team must create the hold via an internal ticket with the signed legal request.

Expedited purge / emergency erase
- We offer an expedited purge path for legally required irrevocable deletion. Requirements: signed purge request from customer legal, Redwood legal approval, and a support ticket (see SUP-3456 pattern).
- Timeline for expedited purge: we can guarantee logical deletion within 24h of approvals. Physical purge depends on where the data resides: on-prem/offsite glacier-like stores may take up to 90 days to reach verifiable zero due to downstream provider retention policies. We will provide a Proof of Deletion certificate at completion.

KMS considerations
- Crypto-erase is our standard secure-erase method: we can render data unreadable by destroying data keys. If you request an expedited purge, we coordinate KMS key schedule to ensure we can generate a PD certificate. Note: if customer-managed keys (BYOK) are used, the customer must also approve key destruction or rotation per the contract.

Action items / proposed dry-run plan
1) We propose a scoped dry-run on a non-prod workspace that mirrors acme-cust-42: run a deletion request, monitor metadata changes, attempt a restore from the latest nightly snapshot, and observe timing until tombstone and sweep hit.
2) Karthik (cc'd) will own the dry-run orchestration and provide a playbook.
3) Please confirm a 1-hour window on May 20th PST for the dry-run.

I've attached our standard delete process doc and a purge request template to this message for your review. If you need us to modify the purge template for Acme's legal format, we can do that.

Attachments: redwood-delete-process.pdf, purge-req-template.docx

Next: Karthik / Evelyn — can you review the timelines and confirm if the 7-day worst-case for Dedicated physical propagation is accurate for your current infra constraints?

Thanks Marcus — a couple quick clarifications from infra:

- The 7-day worst-case figure is accurate for the cross-region compaction path only when offsite cold replicas are involved (we queue GC jobs to reduce load; those jobs may be deprioritized during global maintenance windows). For Dedicated tenants with reserved capacity we can often complete physical compaction within 48–72h if we allocate burst resources.
- Immutable snapshot store (our cold archive) enforces retention at object-level and cannot be modified; snapshots written there will remain until their TTL expires. That means restores from immutable archive may contain data you requested to delete if the snapshot was taken before the delete request.

Karthik — can you draft the dry-run playbook and include exact API calls, expected job ids, and smoke-test checks for restoration success? I'll stand by to open a temporary burst allocation if Acme wants us to expedite the compaction for the run.

Evelyn

Subject: Final: timelines and purge process (dry-run coordination)

Elena — following our internal run-through, here are the confirmed timelines and the playbook we will use for your dry-run on May 20th: please confirm acceptance.

Confirmed timelines (Dedicated / Acme account)
- Logical deletion timeline: immediate metadata tombstone; Console shows object "deleted" within minutes.
- Snapshot visibility: any snapshot created before deletion remains readable until its snapshot TTL (your tenant: 90 days).
- Physical GC (standard path): 48–72h if we allocate burst compaction; otherwise default up to 7 days.
- Cold backup purge (offsite archive): up to 90 days in edge cases due to downstream provider retention.

Emergency purge path (how to request)
1) Submit a signed purge request using attached purge-req-template.docx and open a SUP ticket referencing SUP-3456 style flow.
2) Redwood Legal & Security must approve (we'll respond within 24h of a complete request).
3) We schedule KMS key coordination and confirm if customer-managed keys are involved.
4) Once approvals are complete we run crypto-erase and provide a Proof of Deletion certificate (template attached). Expected confirmation for crypto-erase completion: 7–90 days depending on storage tier.

Dry-run playbook (high level)
- Pre-checks (Day 0): verify non-prod workspace mirror exists; snapshot baseline; verify RBAC tokens.
- Step 1: Submit deletion via API; capture returned job id (example shown in playbook).
- Step 2: Monitor job: metadata state -> tombstone -> sweep eligibility -> GC job start -> GC job completion.
- Step 3: Immediately attempt restore from latest snapshot taken prior to deletion (expected to succeed since snapshot immutability).
- Post-run: Provide timeline log and ask operations to optionally run burst compaction to observe physical GC window.

Deliverables for May 20 run
- Marcus: run coordination and communication with Acme.
- Karthik: dry-run playbook with API examples and a sample script (he will share in the linked Drive folder).
- Evelyn: approve temporary burst compaction allocation if Acme requests faster physical GC.

Please reply with: (A) your approval to run on May 20 at 10:00am PST, (B) whether you want us to exercise the expedited purge flow as part of the run (note: that requires signed legal request and cannot be simulated without approvals).

Attachments: proof-of-deletion-template.csv

Best,
